morning.title: MORTGAGE MARKET MORNING BRIEF
morning.body: Mortgage rates: 7.11% published 2026-11-12, modeled 7.08% today. 10-year Treasury: 5.07% (-3 bp). MBS: 4.10 ticks. Rate bias: Improving. The mortgage spread is 201 bp, normal versus its 208 bp long-run average. Ahead: Initial Jobless Claims on 11-19, Existing Home Sales on 11-22. Biggest risk: no single dominant catalyst. What LOs should know: pull your float list and re-price. Improvements reach rate sheets with a one to two day lag

eod.title: END OF DAY REVIEW
eod.what_moved: Mortgage rates are improving. The 10-year Treasury is 5.07% (-3 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.08%.
eod.why: The 10-year Treasury is at 5.07%, -3 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved -7 bp. That breaks down exactly: +26 bp from Treasuries and -33 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 201 bp, which is normal and sits at the 52th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly -7 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.
eod.reprice_caveat: Real reprice detection needs a live MBS feed. This is inferred from the modeled tick move.
eod.expectations_change: The 2-year barely moved, so Fed expectations are unchanged.
